texts.narrative.move.action: Say what is being done, and which action fixes the control rather than the symptom.
texts.narrative.move.attribution: Say where the movement happened: which unit or line carried it and which held up. The one that moved the result gets the weight; the ones that behaved get a clause.
texts.narrative.move.cause: State the established cause first, then what was believed before it and how that was ruled out.
texts.narrative.move.chronology: Tell what happened in the order it happened, including the explanation that turned out to be wrong.
texts.narrative.move.comparison: Set the section's figures against budget, forecast and, where a prior-period fact is supplied, last month. Let the reader see the size of each gap, and do not restate the headline.
texts.narrative.move.context: Describe the symptom a reader will recognise, so they know within a sentence whether this document applies to them.
texts.narrative.move.decision: Say what the reader is being asked to note or decide, in the first sentence.
texts.narrative.move.driver: Name what moved the result and tie each cause to its figure. Say whether it looks structural or one-off only where the facts or the standing context support it.
texts.narrative.move.headline: Open with the one figure that matters most and say plainly what it means: ahead of plan or behind it, acceptable or not. One or two sentences; the rest of the section earns it.
texts.narrative.move.impact: State the cost in the units the business feels: records, days, the close, money. Keep a calendar impact and a profit impact apart.
texts.narrative.move.implication: Say what the figures already cited mean for this reader. Introduce no new figure; reason from the ones above.
texts.narrative.move.owner: Name who owns the next step, and say plainly where ownership is missing.
texts.narrative.move.procedure: Give the steps in order, in the imperative, so a reader can follow them without understanding the cause.
texts.narrative.move.risk: Name what stays exposed after the fix and what would make the failure recur.
texts.narrative.move.status: Say where things stand now, with the confidence of the moment the author wrote in.
texts.narrative.move.transition: Close with the line that hands the reader to what comes next. No new figure.
texts.narrative.moves.rule.01: Where a request carries `moves`, write one paragraph per move, in the order given, separated by a blank line. Each move says what its paragraph must do and lists the facts it may draw on; a `derived` move introduces no new fact and reasons from the ones already cited.
texts.narrative.moves.rule.02: Every paragraph argues: what moved, why, against what, what it means, what is being done. A paragraph that lists the figures in the order supplied has not made its move, even if every rule above is met.
texts.narrative.moves.rule.03: Where `display_names` gives a subject the name a reader uses, write that name; never write a recorded slug such as a hyphenated service name into prose.
texts.narrative.moves.rule.04: Each move states `sentences`, the fewest its paragraph says (one per thing it measures, up to three, counting neither a prior-period figure nor a fact an earlier section already said; a derived move one), and the request's `floor` states the least the section says in total: `sentences` across `paragraphs`. A section below its floor is refused as section_floor; give each fact its sentence rather than packing several into one. A `floor` carrying `exempt` has fewer facts than moves and no floor: do not pad it.

texts.narrative.section_moves.template:
Write the "{section}" section of a {artifact_type} for {audience}.

What this section has to do:
{purpose}

You are writing as: {author_title}{persona}
Voice: {voice}{traits}
Target length: about {target_words} words, as several paragraphs of connected prose.
You know only what had been recorded and was available to this author at: {cutoff}

Write it move by move. Each move is one paragraph, in this order, and each
paragraph argues rather than lists: what moved, why, against what, what it
means, what is being done.
{moves}

Facts you may use. Reference each one as {{fact:ID}}; never write a figure out:
{facts}

Where a fact carries "prior period: FACT-ID", both are available to cite. That is
how a trend is stated: reference this period and the last, and let the reader see
the movement.

Subjects a reader names differently from the record (use the reader's name):
{display}

Where each subject sits:
{hierarchy}

Standing context. This explains why the figures look as they do. Reason from it
and allude to it; do not assert it as a finding and do not cite it:
{background}

Terminology guidance:
{terminology}

You must not claim:
{forbidden}
{feedback}
Rules:
- No digits anywhere outside a {{fact:ID}} reference; the check is lexical.
  Spell any other number (an ordinal, a count) out in words, or leave it out.
- Every assertion must be supported by at least one of the facts above.
- Every fact reference in prose must also be cited by a claim.
- Do not mention anything not present in the facts above.
- Facts marked REQUIRED must appear.
- A fact whose validity had ended by your cut-off is a past belief. Tell it as
  history, never as the current position.
- One paragraph per move, separated by a blank line. Do not head the paragraphs.
- Weight the facts. The line that moved the result gets the paragraph; the lines
  that behaved get a clause.

Return the prose, and a list of the claims it makes with the fact IDs supporting each.
texts.narrative.spelling.rule.01: Figures are spelled for a reader. A reference to a money fact prints its currency, a rounded magnitude and its direction ('AUD 10.2m adverse', 'AUD 958k', 'nil'); a percentage prints with '%'; a date prints in words. So write no unit word, currency code or direction word beside a reference: '{{fact:ID}} thousands', 'AUD {{fact:ID}}' and '{{fact:ID}} adverse adverse' are refused as number_spelling.
texts.narrative.spelling.rule.02: Say a direction once. When the reference's own clause already carries it, in a phrase ('a shortfall of', 'a gap of') or a direction word before or just after it ('missing plan by', 'fell by', 'overspent by', '... below budget'), the reference drops its own 'adverse'; do not add it back. A clause that says the other way ('ahead of plan by' an adverse figure) is refused as number_spelling: the figure went the other way. A zero money figure prints as 'nil', so give it a sentence that reads with that word ('the effect on the result was {{fact:ID}}').
texts.narrative.spelling.rule.03: Never type a recorded identifier: a snake_case value ('control_failure'), a service slug ('inventory-valuation') or a raw enum from a fact. Reference the fact, whose value prints in words, or write the words `display_names` and the finding give; an identifier in your own words is refused as slug_leak.
